title: Jump Game
statement: You start at index 0 of `nums`. The value `nums[i]` is the **maximum** jump length from index `i`. Return `True` if the last index can be reached.

example.why: Every route ends up on index 3, whose jump length is 0. Index 4 can never be reached.

idea: It does not matter *how* we get somewhere, only **how far we can get at all**. Keep one number: `max_reachable`, the farthest index reachable so far.
Walk through the indexes in order. If index `i` is within reach, then everything up to `i + nums[i]` is within reach too — update `max_reachable`.
If we ever arrive at an index **beyond** `max_reachable`, there is a gap nobody can jump over → `False`. If the loop finishes, every index (including the last) was reachable → `True`.

complexity.timeWhy: One pass over the array; each index is looked at once.

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [3,2,1,0,4]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`max_reachable` is the farthest index we know how to reach. At the start that is index 0, where we stand.
Index 0 is reachable, and from it we can jump up to 3 → as far as index 3. That is farther than before: `max_reachable` = **3**.
Index 1 is reachable, but from it we get at most to index 1 + 2 = 3 — no farther than the 3 we already have.
Index 2 is reachable, but from it we get at most to index 2 + 1 = 3 — no farther than the 3 we already have.
Index 3 is reachable, but from it we get at most to index 3 + 0 = 3 — no farther than the 3 we already have.
Index 4 lies **beyond** the farthest reachable index (3). Nothing can get us here — or past it.
The last index cannot be reached → **False**.
Done — the answer is **`False`**. Every route ends up on index 3, whose jump length is 0. Index 4 can never be reached.
